fact_label: Remote work for a foreign employer/clients has no legal visa or work-permit category
value_raw: No official authorization exists — "No visa or permit category covers ordinary remote work for overseas clients"
notes: New fact, 2026-07-18 ([specialist], thinnest-3-criteria wave) — Income viability carried zero fact rows before, a genuine gap now closed with the single most load-bearing finding in it. Vietnam's Labor Code (Law 45/2019/QH14), Article 151, requires foreign nationals "working in Vietnam" to hold a valid work permit unless an Article 154 exemption applies; the source states plainly no e-visa work category exists and that "officers can ask about your activity." Divergence flag set Confirmed-diverges (not Not-yet-checked) because the same source explicitly documents the paper-vs-practice gap itself, not just the legal mechanism: in practice, many long-stay remote workers use the e-visa (or a visa exemption) and work online for employers/clients outside Vietnam, and when the 90 days end, cross into a neighboring country for a short trip before returning on a fresh e-visa — but, in the source's own words, "None of this is legal certainty" and "the rules have tightened before." Working without a required permit carries a fine of VND 15-25 million plus expulsion. CITATION-INTEGRITY PASS 2026-08-24 ([specialist]): re-fetched asialongstay.com directly, multiple differently-worded passes. CONFIRMED verbatim: "No visa or permit category covers ordinary remote work for overseas clients"; "officers can ask about your activity" (part of "Vietnamese law has no e-visa work category, and officers can ask about your activity"); "working in Vietnam" (part of "Article 151 requires foreign nationals working in Vietnam to hold a valid work permit"); "None of this is legal certainty" and "the rules have tightened before" (each individually verbatim, though from two non-adjacent sentences in the source with other material between them — the prior notes field spliced them into one continuous quoted string without an ellipsis, which read as more contiguous than the source actually is; fixed here by reporting each as its own short quote rather than one stitched sentence). fact_label: Temporary Residence Card (TRC) via Registered Investment — capital threshold
unit: USD, lump-sum registered-investment capital, roughly (VND 3,000,000,000 — the ĐT3-tier floor — converted at ~26,200 VND/USD, 2026-08-09)
notes: RESEARCHED 2026-08-11 ([specialist]; ask: [specialist]/our records recount, our records): the prior [GAP] was a real research miss, not a genuine legal absence — Vietnam's investor-visa/Temporary Residence Card (TRC) structure IS tiered, same shape as Thailand's, it simply wasn't found in the 2026-07-11 first pass. Governing law: Article 8 of Law No. 51/2019/QH14 (amending Law No. 47/2014/QH13 on entry/exit/transit/residence of foreigners), which defines four investor-visa symbols by capital contribution (vốn góp): ĐT1 ≥VND100 billion (~$3.8M), ĐT2 VND50–<100 billion (~$1.9M–$3.8M), ĐT3 VND3–<50 billion (~$114,500–$1.9M), ĐT4 <VND3 billion (~<$114,500). CRITICAL finding for this specific route/fact: cross-corroborated across 5 independent sources that ĐT4 (the bottom tier, under ~$114,500) receives only a 12-month DT visa and is NOT eligible for a Temporary Residence Card at all — the TRC itself (this fact's own subject) only becomes available at ĐT3 and above, i.e. the real floor for 'TRC via Registered Investment' as a route is VND 3,000,000,000 (~$114,500 at the cited rate), not zero and not undocumented. Above that floor, ĐT3 grants a TRC up to 3 years (some sources say up to 10 years once combined with the visa's own renewal path — sources disagree on the exact TRC ceiling for ĐT3 specifically, see the companion tier-structure row), ĐT2/ĐT1 grant longer TRCs (5-10 years) for larger capital — those upper tiers affect duration, not whether the TRC route applies at all. Sourcing: cross-corroborated across 68solutions.vn, vietnam-visa.com, emerhub.com, tanvanlang.com, and accgroup.vn (which quotes the verbatim Vietnamese statutory text of Điều 8: 'ĐT3 – Cấp cho nhà đầu tư nước ngoài tại Việt Nam ... có vốn góp giá trị từ 03 tỷ đồng đến dưới 50 tỷ đồng'), all five independently converging on the same VND figures. PRIMARY-SOURCE CHECK ATTEMPTED, NOT REACHABLE: thuvienphapluat.vn (403 Forbidden), vbpl.vn (404), vanban.chinhphu.vn (page loads but only shows metadata, not article text), pbgdpl.moj.gov.vn PDF (socket closed / unreachable via fetch tool) — all four primary Vietnamese legal-database/government sources were checked directly and found inaccessible this pass, not skipped; confidence rests on cross-corroboration across five independent professional-advisory sources, one of which quotes the primary statutory text verbatim, not on a direct primary-source fetch. FX conversion (VND→USD) is this specialist's own computed conversion using a dated, cited rate (exchange-rates.org, ~26,200 VND/USD as of 2026-08-09), not a source-provided USD figure — flagged per our records discipline; the VND figure is the real legal number, the USD figure is a derived estimate that will drift with the exchange rate. Divergence flag set to 'Not yet checked' (was 'N/A' in error on the prior gap row) — no lived account of an actual DT3+ investor's real TRC-issuance experience found this pass. Verification Review 2026-08-25 ([specialist]): re-fetched accgroup.vn directly tonight -- the DT1-DT4 VND capital boundaries (>=100bn / 50-<100bn / 3-<50bn / <3bn) read back verbatim-matching this row's own figures. Confirmed accurate. Also re-checked the VND/USD conversion rate used here (26,200 as of 2026-08-09) against current August 2026 rates (26,060-26,280 across multiple trackers, essentially unchanged -- no material FX drift). The ~$114,500 USD figure remains accurate to within normal daily FX noise; [specialist] moderate currency-staleness flag does not bite on this particular threshold.

fact_label: Temporary Residence Card (TRC) via Registered Investment — full ĐT1-ĐT4 tier structure
value_raw: ĐT1 ≥VND100bn (~$3.8M): visa up to 5yr, Temporary Residence Card (TRC) up to 10yr. ĐT2 VND50-<100bn (~$1.9-3.8M): visa up to 5yr, TRC up to 5yr (one source: 10yr). ĐT3 VND3-<50bn (~$114.5k-1.9M): visa up to 3yr, TRC up to 2-3yr (one source: 10yr — sources disagree on ĐT3's TRC ceiling specifically). ĐT4 <VND3bn (~<$114.5k): visa only, up to 12 months, no TRC.
notes: Companion descriptive row to the threshold row above — carries the full tiered structure for a reader whose capital exceeds the ĐT3 floor and wants to know what a larger investment buys in Temporary Residence Card (TRC) duration. Confidence held at Medium (one notch below the threshold row's High) because sources genuinely disagree on ĐT2's and ĐT3's exact TRC ceiling (5yr vs 10yr for ĐT2; 2-3yr vs 10yr for ĐT3) even though they agree completely on the capital-tier VND boundaries and on ĐT4's no-TRC exclusion. Alternative qualification path noted by sources but not independently verified: investing in a Vietnamese-government-designated priority/encouraged sector can reportedly qualify for a higher tier at a lower capital figure — not confirmed with a primary source, flagged as a real open question, not folded into the headline threshold. fact_label: Temporary Residence Card (TRC) via Registered Investment converts to permanent residency
value_raw: No
notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-22 ([specialist]; ask: [specialist], our records, sole remaining data_gap cause for marek/waldo x VN both grains). Read Article 39 of Law No. 47/2014/QH13 (Vietnam's governing entry/exit/transit/residence law) directly and verbatim, not via aggregator paraphrase: permanent residence is considered for exactly four statutory categories -- (1) foreigners awarded medals/titles by the Vietnamese government for contributions to Vietnam's development/protection, (2) foreign scientists/experts residing in Vietnam (requires a ministerial proposal per Article 40.2), (3) a foreigner sponsored by a parent/spouse/child who is a Vietnamese citizen with permanent residence (this category carries the sourced 3-consecutive-years-of-temporary-residence eligibility clock, Article 40.3 -- notably this clock applies ONLY to the family-sponsored category, not generically to any TRC holder), and (4) stateless persons with Vietnamese temporary residence dating to 2000 or earlier. Foreign investors (the DT visa/TRC category, any tier DT1-DT4) are not named in any of the four categories -- investor status is not merely a slower or conditional path to permanent residence (PR), it is genuinely excluded from the permanent-residence law entirely. An investor's TRC, however long its own validity runs (up to 10 years at the DT1 tier per the companion capital-tier-structure row), does not itself accrue toward or qualify for permanent residence. Primary-source access: thuvienphapluat.vn, vbpl.vn, and vanban.chinhphu.vn were all checked directly again this pass and found unreachable, same pattern as the 2026-08-11 threshold pass on this same route. The verbatim statutory text was instead obtained via the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs' Hanoi embassy consular portal (hanoi-be.mfa.gov.tr), which hosts a full English-translation PDF of Law 47/2014/QH13 -- a foreign government's own hosted translation of the Vietnamese statute, not Vietnam's own government portal, but genuine verbatim article text read directly (not an aggregator's summary), the strongest source reached this pass. Cross-corroborated by luatvietnam.vn's own 2025 'Vietnam Golden Visa' legal-news summary, which independently states ordinary investors are not among the permanent-residence-eligible categories. One flagged, unresolved wrinkle: one secondary legal-directory search result described Article 39 as 'amended by Law No. 51/2019/QH14' -- but a direct fetch of 51/2019/QH14's own text (the same amending law that created the DT1-DT4 investor tiers) found no permanent-residence content in it at all, suggesting that 2019 amendment touched only visa/TRC provisions, not Articles 39-41; the 'as amended' attribution in that one secondary source was not independently chased further (would require reading 51/2019/QH14's full amendment list article-by-article). Does not change the finding either way: no version of this law, amended or not, was found anywhere this pass to list investors as PR-eligible. Divergence flag set to 'Not yet checked': this is a clean statutory-exclusion finding (a route simply isn't on the eligible list), not a discretionary provision where enforcement could plausibly diverge from text, but no lived account of an investor attempting and being refused PR was sought or found this pass. Verification Review 2026-08-25 ([specialist]): reviewed under this review -- no re-check needed beyond what the 2026-08-22 pass already did (verbatim primary-source statutory text read directly, the strongest sourcing standard this project uses); flagged here only to close this row out of the registry's non-quoted checklist, not because anything new was found.
